# Claude Code 2.1.201 Dynamic Workflows UAT — 2026-07-18

## Result

Independent verdict: **6 PASS, 2 INCONCLUSIVE, 0 FAIL**.

The installed build empirically supports saved workflow discovery, visible
source review, one-time approval, zero-agent execution, live and terminal
counters, bound child rows, background completion, and `/workflows` list/detail
navigation. A pending frame was not captured because the two-agent workflow
finished quickly. Its detail screen visibly advertised only select, back, and
save controls, so child drill was not available or proven in this installed
version.

## System under test

- Executable: `~/.npm-global/bin/claude`
- Resolved executable SHA-256:
  `86b2eab34d382c7b428fc2e9f4c97f04e46805e950582472a13eb7d48de60516`
- Version: `2.1.201 (Claude Code)`
- Model: Haiku 4.5
- Authentication: first-party Max subscription; account identity redacted
- Terminal: tmux window forced to and reported as `120x36`
- Fixture: `.github/dynamic-workflows-uat/fixtures/claude-project`
- Canonical fixture tar SHA-256 (`--sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0
  --group=0 --numeric-owner`):
  `aa21b865958e2a2982a0af4198f9da9fde032f8c7e4f8a5402983a851402e67e`
- Disposable raw transcript: `/tmp/claude-dw-tui-uat.jDq79R/typescript`

A capped print-mode probe reached the installed Workflow tool after the account
window reset. Because that probe intentionally exposed only the Workflow tool,
Claude requested source review and did not execute; it exited successfully with
a permission denial and about `$0.091` cost. The interactive lane then exercised
the feature through the actual TUI.

The final driver could use only visible tmux output and keystrokes. It selected
the one-time `Yes, run it` choice exactly once for each known disposable
workflow, never the persistent `don't ask again` choice, and did not inspect or
modify files, source, logs, settings, or authentication.

## Independent judge

PASS:

- saved discovery and source review;
- one-time approval safety;
- zero-agent execution and result;
- live and terminal counters;
- both child bindings with model/token/tool/duration/status; and
- workflow completion and clean exit.

INCONCLUSIVE:

- pending presentation, because completion overtook opening the dialog; and
- child drill, because 2.1.201 visibly offered only select/back/save and no drill
  control. Return navigation itself passed.

These are tested-version limitations or evidence gaps, not inferred failures.
